title: Minimum-motion equiluminance (Anstis & Cavanagh 1983)
summary: When red and green have equal effective brightness, a four-frame colour sequence loses its consistent apparent motion. Judge its direction or adjust the colour balance to find that point; compare it with minimum flicker. The match is specific to the observer, stimulus and calibrated display, not a colour-vision diagnosis.
references: Anstis, S. M., & Cavanagh, P. (1983). A minimum motion technique for judging equiluminance. In J. D. Mollon & L. T. Sharpe (Eds.), Colour vision: Physiology and psychophysics (pp. 155-166). London: Academic Press.

deviations.original: Computer-controlled colour TV, P22 phosphors (red x 0.68 y 0.32, green x 0.28 y 0.60, blue x 0.15 y 0.07), luminances read with a Spectra photometer (p. 157)
deviations.here: Any gamma-linearised display; luminances in cd/m2 computed from a per-rig photometry file (each gun at full drive). The colours are the display's primaries, not P22 chromaticities
deviations.reason: Modern displays have no P22 phosphors; luminance matching only needs the guns' luminances. A display's own primaries change what 'red' and 'green' are, so settings do not transfer between displays

deviations.original: Light/dark yellow made by dithering pairs of the 512 raster lines between the red and green of the colour grating within each bar (p. 156)
deviations.here: By default every pixel shows the additive mean of the two colours (interleave_mix: additive); the paper's dither is available as line_dither with dither_rows rows per band
deviations.reason: On an additive, linearised display the mean is the same light as the spatially summed dither, without depending on raster lines being below resolution on a modern panel

deviations.here: The display's own white point (all three guns at equal drive)
deviations.reason: A display's white is what it has; matching to x 0.30 y 0.30 would need a spectroradiometer and changes nothing in the method

deviations.original: Fig. 1 shows each grating displaced rightward from its predecessor; the paper does not say whether the direction varied
deviations.here: Each condition is run with rightward and with leftward quarter-cycle steps equally often; reports are scored as 'test lighter' (motion in the step direction), 'reference lighter' or 'neither'
deviations.reason: Separates the luminance judgement from a bias to answer left or right

deviations.original: Left, right or neither (p. 157); how reports were given is not stated
deviations.here: LEFT, RIGHT and DOWN arrow keys while the cycle runs
deviations.reason: A keyboard is on every rig

deviations.here: Scroll wheel or UP/DOWN arrows, 1% per step, SPACE to commit
deviations.reason: Joysticks are not standard rig hardware

deviations.here: Period rounded to a multiple of 4 pixels (snap_period_to_pixels) so every step is exactly a quarter cycle; the effective frequency is recorded per trial
deviations.reason: A quarter-cycle step that is not whole pixels would change the phase relation the method depends on

deviations.here: A real-data session with display_calibration: calibrated is refused unless the photometry file says measured: true; uncalibrated-demo runs and labels every trial as nominal, device-specific values
deviations.reason: So no one reports cd/m2 that were never measured

deviations.here: adjust-red-green.yaml: Experiment 1's red/green stimulus set by adjustment, the practical calibration use the paper recommends (p. 165)
deviations.reason: Labelled as not one of the paper's conditions

deviations.original: Minimum flicker measured at 7.5 and 15 Hz only (p. 161)
deviations.here: No separate temporal-frequency flicker file; min-flicker-adjust takes any rates_hz
deviations.reason: The paper's own flicker settings were impossible below 7.5 Hz; the motion task carries Experiment 3

tasks.title: Minimum flicker, counterphase gratings vs spatial frequency (Experiment 2)
tasks.summary: Fixation mark, then a square-wave grating whose bars swap between the colour and grey (two frames each, 15 Hz) while the observer turns the colour's luminance until flicker is least, and presses SPACE.

parameters.name: field
parameters.label: Field
parameters.meaning: counterphase: a square-wave grating whose bars swap between the test colour and grey (p. 159).

parameters.name: reference_cd_m2
parameters.label: Reference luminance
parameters.meaning: Grey luminance (paper: 13.6 cd/m2, p. 159).

parameters.name: test_colours
parameters.label: Test colours
parameters.meaning: Colours matched to grey (paper: red, green, blue).

parameters.name: rates_hz
parameters.label: Flicker rates
parameters.meaning: Full flicker cycles per second (paper: 15 Hz, two 60-Hz frames per state).

parameters.name: spatial_freqs_cpd
parameters.label: Spatial frequencies
parameters.meaning: Square-wave frequencies (paper: 0.625-5 c/deg).

parameters.name: step_factor
parameters.label: Knob step
parameters.meaning: Factor per wheel notch or arrow press. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: adjust_timeout
parameters.label: Setting deadline
parameters.meaning: A setting not committed in this time is served again. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: paradigm.n_per_condition
parameters.label: Settings per condition and step
parameters.meaning: 3 x 2 = six readings (paper, p. 159); the step sets which bars are test-coloured first.

parameters.name: patch_size_dva
parameters.label: Patch size
parameters.meaning: Side of the square grating patch in a dark surround. ASSUMED: Experiments 2-3 do not restate it; Experiment 1's 2 x 2 deg.

parameters.name: fixation.square_arcmin
parameters.label: Fixation square
parameters.meaning: Side of the blue fixation square (paper: 6 arcmin).

parameters.name: fixation.cross_arcmin
parameters.label: Fixation cross span
parameters.meaning: Length of the white cross arms. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: fixation.line_arcmin
parameters.label: Fixation cross line
parameters.meaning: Line width of the white cross. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: photometry_file
parameters.label: Photometry file
parameters.meaning: Rig file with each gun's full-drive luminance. The example is NOT a measurement; luminances computed from it are device-specific demonstration values.

parameters.name: display_calibration
parameters.label: Calibration mode
parameters.meaning: calibrated: a real-data session needs a measured photometry file. uncalibrated-demo: runs anyway and labels every trial as nominal, device-specific values.

parameters.name: snap_period_to_pixels
parameters.label: Whole-pixel quarter cycles
parameters.meaning: Round the grating period to a multiple of 4 px so every step is exactly a quarter cycle; the effective spatial frequency is recorded. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: fixation_duration
parameters.label: Fixation period
parameters.meaning: Fixation mark alone before the stimulus starts. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: iti
parameters.label: Inter-trial interval
parameters.meaning: Dark interval between trials. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

outcomes.name: TIMEOUT
outcomes.meaning: No setting in time; served again.
